# What Java's ImageIO makes of every JPEG fixture in `crates/audiveris-jpeg`,
# plus the corpus page. Generated by `oracle/java/JpegVerdicts.java`, JDK 21.0.10.
#
# Audiveris reads JPEGs through this reader, so this file -- not libjpeg-turbo --
# is the authority on parity. `tests/parity.rs` also runs libjpeg-turbo, which is
# faster and localizes a disagreement to the sample; but the two libjpegs are not
# the same library, and on damaged input they disagree with each other. Where
# they do, this file wins and `tests/parity.rs` records the exception.
#
# The hash pins what a file decodes to; the accept/reject pins whether it decodes
# at all, which no sample comparison can see. Four fixtures here exist only
# because differential fuzzing found us accepting files Audiveris refuses.
#
# <path> <TAB> accept <width> <height> <bands> <fnv1a64 of the raster, row-major>
# <path> <TAB> reject <ImageIO message>
